design_rationale:
# Task 0 — design rationale (rework round 3)

## 0. Draw and scope
- draw_counts.py --task 0: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 6, 5] (multiset). Tree: pos_ext_payoff_quote (root, 6 factors, user tool pay_off_plan_f18fb847) <- pos_ext_late_fee_relief (5, agent relieve_late_fee_b1a4bf3c) and <- pos_ext_returned_fee_relief (5, agent relieve_returned_payment_fee_3fbe4785), which itself waits on the late-fee relief.
- Round 3 change: the make-up reliefs replace the make-good reversal (no fractional extent; a relief is owed only once the missed payment was made up after the fee, or the returned payment replaced after the return, and the make-up has cleared). The late fee and returned-payment fee schedules moved to task 1 with the payment reset; scopes are disjoint and cover all six policies.

## 1. Why this is a good test
Renata asks only to pay her Lakeshore Family Dental plan off today. Two system-owed writes are missing: the courtesy-basis make-up relief of the 2026-09-21 late fee (the 2026-09-10 payment was made up on 2026-10-13, cleared on 2026-10-16) and the relief of the 23.28 fee of the payment that came back R02 on 2026-10-06 (replaced on 2026-10-13). The payoff rule waits on both in state form. The agent must size each relief (capped size by the return or late-fee record, timing, AutoPay or principal share, personal-loan and FlexLine history), then quote a payoff whose interest since the 2026-09-19 closing is split at the 2026-10-13 payment, which leaves out the 60.00 provider credit still to post, and whose good-through period is built from four hold rules, and hand the payment to her.

## 2. Problem-tree card
| edge | kind | gate | form | prerequisite sentence | condition | resolved by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| payoff -> late-fee relief | value_input | plan_bal | state | "A payoff amount is worked out only after the plan's ledger carries the late-fee relief owed on the plan's latest late fee under the make-up relief schedules." | when a relief above 0.00 is owed on the latest late fee, a waiver entry names it | relieve_late_fee_b1a4bf3c (agent) |
| payoff -> returned-fee relief | value_input | plan_bal | state | "A payoff amount is not worked out until the plan's ledger carries the returned-payment-fee relief owed on the fee of the plan's latest returned payment." | when a relief above 0.00 is owed on the latest return's fee, a waiver entry names it | relieve_returned_payment_fee_3fbe4785 (agent) |
| returned-fee relief -> late-fee relief | value_input | same_due_late_relieved | state | "A returned-payment-fee relief is set only after the plan's ledger carries the late-fee relief owed on the plan's latest late fee, which takes a last remaining courtesy waiver first when it is above 0.00." | when a late-fee relief above 0.00 is owed on the latest late fee, a waiver entry names it | relieve_late_fee_b1a4bf3c (agent) |
- Each condition is producible in every reachable case: a relief that works out to 0.00 is not owed and nothing is booked, so the condition holds vacuously; the two records are told apart by the fee entry they name (a late-fee entry or a returned-payment fee entry), and both count as courtesy waivers within the plan's limit, as the restated courtesy sentence says, the returned-fee relief's own rule fixing the priority (the last remaining waiver going to the late-fee relief when one above 0.00 is owed, otherwise to the returned-payment-fee relief).

## 3. Factors (tiers taken on this world)
- late-fee relief: size capped (two returns within 6 months); timing 22 days -> 0.9; AutoPay debits 3 -> 0.95; loan return within 12 months -> 0.9; FlexLine return -> 0.95. Result 7.31 (baseline 18.62).
- returned-fee relief: size capped (the late fee of the same missed payment already carries the late-fee relief; without it the keep-back size gives 12.66); timing 7 days -> 0.9; principal 3615.65 -> 0.9; loan 0.9; FlexLine 0.95. Result 8.31 (baseline 23.28).
- payoff: split interest; credit still to post 60.00 left out; holds 10 + 3 + 2 + 1 days. Result 3920.45 (baseline 3955.67).
- Multi-source: the loan and FlexLine factors combine returns and late fees; cross-difficulty: loan and line factors read the personal-loan and FlexLine ledgers seeded for her.

## 4. Seeded history and traps
- The 2026-08-26 return (R01) reversed a 200.00 payment beyond the payment due; it carries an 8.82 fee and is never replaced (no due date), so no relief is owed on it and it does not use her courtesy allowance.
- Two payments share 2026-10-13 (equal amounts): the payoff's split adds back both; the reliefs read the payment recorded first toward each due date.
- The dispute is resolved with a credit, not open: the late-fee relief and the payoff read it differently (the relief not at all; the payoff leaves the credit still to post out).
- 48-Month Reduced APR plan: two courtesy waivers per 12 months, none used, so both reliefs fit within the limit in either order.

## 4b. Round 4
- The make-up test reads the plan's next due date and the payment entries (a return is matched to the payment it names), never a due date on a return row; the payoff's split adds back every payment of the latest payment date; money results round half up; the plan's courtesy limit binds both reliefs, and a last remaining waiver goes to the late-fee relief only when one above 0.00 is owed (round 6); since round 9 the returned-fee relief waits on the late-fee relief in state form instead of recomputing it.

## 4c. Round 10
- The returned-fee relief's size reads whether the late fee of the same missed payment already carries a waiver, so its wait on the late-fee relief changes its scored amount on this world (8.31 with the relief booked, 12.66 without).

## 4d. Round 11
- Both relief size ladders are monotone at every fee: the capped tier is the keep-back figure but never more than the cap, so a worse record never gives a larger relief; task 0's sizes and the returned-fee relief's 12.66 skip figure are unchanged.

## 4e. Round 12
- The payoff rule now states that the amount left out for billing disputes comes off the payoff amount only, never off the interest-bearing balance; the courtesy priority between the reliefs is stated only in the returned-fee relief's rule (the waiting side); the returned-payment fee's scope sentence no longer carries factor wording.

## 5. Gold
reads (11) -> relieve_late_fee_b1a4bf3c 7.31 (step 12) -> relieve_returned_payment_fee_3fbe4785 8.31 (step 14) -> pay_off_plan_f18fb847 3920.45 from UW 3741 (step 16, customer).
user_scenario:
You are Renata Lindqvist, 39, a project coordinator in Madison, Wisconsin, calling Larkspur Lending on a Friday morning between meetings. You talk quickly and plainly, a little apologetic about how messy your autumn finances have been, and you like to get to the point. A work bonus landed this week and you want your PracticePay plan from Lakeshore Family Dental — the one you opened for your dental implant in April — paid off in full today so it is simply gone. That is the whole reason for the call: pay it off now, in one payment, yourself. You do not want a new payment schedule, you do not want anything mailed, and you are not asking about any other account.

You open by saying you would like to pay off your Lakeshore Family Dental financing plan today, all of it, and you give the mobile number on your profile, 6085553417, so they can find you. It is the only PracticePay plan you have.

When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, 1987-03-22, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 3862. If they want something else you can also give your email, renata.lindqvist@gmail.com, or your ZIP code, 53711. You hand these over one or two at a time as they are asked for, not all at once.

You do not know the exact balance and you have no figure of your own in mind; you are relying on the agent to tell you what it takes to pay the plan off today. If the agent asks how you want to pay, or from which account, you explain that you moved your banking to UW Credit Union this month and you want to pay from your UW Credit Union checking account ending in 3741; your old Summit Credit Union account is closed and must not be used. Only if the agent asks about your bank change do you add that you closed the Summit account at the start of October and caught the plan up from UW on Tuesday.

Only if the agent brings up the billing dispute you raised with the dental office about being overcharged, you say the office told you this week that they agreed to credit it back, and that is all you know about it. You do not bring up any fees, earlier payments or anything else on your own; you leave the account details to the agent.

If the agent explains that something has to be put on the plan or sorted out on their side before the payoff figure is final, you say that is fine and they can go ahead. When the agent gives you the payoff amount and sets up the payment for you to complete, you make the payment yourself from the UW Credit Union checking account, for the plan they named and the exact amount they told you, and you read back the confirmation you get. If the agent mentions that any small amount left over after the final interest is worked out comes back to you, you say that is fine.

Once the agent confirms the payment went through, you thank them, say that is everything you needed, and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
